Case name: Erie v. Pap's AM

Opinion filed: 2000-03-29

Case holding summaries:
• stating that asserted interest in combating secondary effects associated with nude dancing are undeniable important
• concluding that, in order to comply with ordinance, requirement that dancers wear pasties and G-strings leaves ample capacity to convey the dancer's erotic message
• statute regulating public nudity properly evaluated as content-neutral because the legislature's "interest in combating the secondary effects associated with [nude dancing] clubs is unrelated to the suppression of the erotic message conveyed by nude dancing"
• stating that the government's interest in combating harmful secondary effects is not related to the suppression of expression
• reasoning that the ordinance "does not target nudity that contains an erotic message; rather, it bans all public nudity, regardless of whether that nudity is accompanied by expressive activity"
• observing that case is moot when issues presented no longer constitute live controversy or when parties are without legal interest in outcome
• holding that Erie's public indecency ordinance is a content-neutral regulation that is a valid restriction on public nudity
• relying on the negative secondary effects doctrine to uphold a city's ordinance as applied to an erotic dancing establishment
• reasonable expectation of recurrence even though strip club owner sold strip club and was no longer involved in nude dancing industry
• rejecting language of preamble of local ordinance as definitive for First Amendment challenge
• concluding that law banning public nude dancing was content-neutral and constitutional
